Native rows ref10_nine_backspace, ref10_nine_ref1_zero and ref10_zero_backspace (API 62.0/67.0, anonymous/isTest) expose an existing matcher mismatch outside literal split eligibility.
Salesforce reduces \10 to \1 followed by 0 when nine captures exist, and never matches \10 with no captures. The current regexp2 engine interprets both as octal backspace. Explicit \010 remains an octal escape in both runtimes.
These 12 native cells are retained in org.tsv. Tests check their split/replaceAll/matcher route equivalence and public group counts; they are not counted as native matches. The other 88 native cells are asserted exactly, including \1 through \9 with minimal/ten captures and \10 with ten captures on matching and octal-looking nonmatching input.
The reported literal fast-path regression is independent: with ten captures the matcher already agrees with Salesforce, while the optimization parses \10 as Go octal. Excluding numeric references repairs the three split routes without changing the older matcher behavior.
